quotes.text: Service accounts sabotage your flows because they conflate human authentication with machine tasks, invite over privilege, erase attribution, and collapse the second conditional access evolves.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Names the four concrete failure modes of service-account-based email flows in one sentence.

quotes.text: Client credentials flows aren't subject to user MFA. That's not a loophole, it's the design. You enforce safety at the permission layer and the policy fence, not with interactive challenges.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Explains why app-only auth is a deliberate security model, not an MFA bypass.

quotes.text: The one misstep that silently exposes every mailbox is skipping the application access policy because mail send is already least privileged. It isn't, without the policy your app can impersonate the tenant's entire directory.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Pinpoints the single configuration gap that turns Mail.Send into tenant-wide impersonation.

quotes.text: Respect retry after globally. When you get throttled, slow the entire worker, not just one thread. Your goal isn't maximum throughput, it's guaranteed delivery without collateral damage.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Gives a clear operational rule for handling Graph throttling.

takeaways: Service accounts with shared passwords, Send As rights and MFA exemptions make Power Automate email flows fragile, over-privileged and impossible to audit cleanly.
An app registration with Mail.Send application permission, authenticated via client credentials and fenced by an Exchange Online application access policy, can only send from approved mailboxes.
Wrapping the Graph call in a custom connector with client request IDs, normalized errors, throttling-aware retries and idempotency keys gives every flow traceable, reliable delivery.
hook: HR notifications, offer letters and policy updates sent through service accounts break at the next MFA prompt or password expiry and leave an unclear audit trail. This episode shows Power Platform and Microsoft 365 admins how to move email flows to an app registration, Microsoft Graph and application access policies, so every message is scoped, reliable and provable.
